messages:
Ana: Hey team — we need a concise post-incident follow-up to send to the 3 Dedicated customers impacted by the latency spike this morning. Incident window I have is ~10:12–10:45 UTC; customers saw tail latency and a few timed-out requests. Can we assemble: short timeline, customer impact (what they saw), root cause summary (high-level), immediate mitigations we executed, and planned preventative actions? Also need an SLA credit estimate. :wave:

Devon: I can pull the on-call timeline + logs. Quick notes: autoscaler missed a burst because a recent policy change tightened the scale-in cooldown, so pool temporarily underprovisioned during a traffic surge. We reverted the cooldown at 10:28 and manually bumped one reserved pool at 10:31 which brought latencies down. :gear:

IncidentBot: [ALERT] Incident #INC-2024-147: Elevated tail latency on Dedicated cluster eu-west-1. Started 2024-06-12T10:12:13Z. Paging routed to @Devon, @Ravi. Status: mitigated 2024-06-12T10:45:02Z.

Ravi: Adding logs excerpt and short RCA draft — rough draft below, feel free to edit for customer-facing phrasing.

```
RCA (technical):
- Trigger: sudden traffic spike from a single customer workload with many concurrent long sequences.
- Failure mode: autoscaler cooldown and a config mismatch prevented timely allocation of additional GPU workers; KV cache pressure increased, causing slower token generation and occasional request timeouts.
- Immediate fix: reverted cooldown change, scaled reserved pool by +2 instances, applied targeted cache eviction to free memory.
```

Maya: This is helpful. For customers we should be explicit about what happened (they saw high tail latency and some 5xx/timeouts) but avoid excessive internal detail. Proposed customer-facing paragraph: "Between 10:12 and 10:45 UTC we experienced an infrastructure issue that temporarily increased response times for Dedicated workloads in eu-west-1. Our engineers implemented mitigations and service returned to normal at ~10:45 UTC. We’ve identified the root cause and are taking actions to reduce the chance of recurrence." Can we get a one-line impact summary for each customer (requests/time windows)?

Ana: Yes — I'll map per-customer telemetry. Quick ask: include a short list of preventative actions and an estimated SLA credit. Also add contact for escalation (Maya + CS team).

Devon: Per-customer notes (rough):
- customer A: ~1.2k requests affected, noticeable latency 10:12–10:33, 12 request timeouts.
- customer B: burst at 10:14, ~45 requests timed out (long sequences).
- customer C: degraded performance for 33 minutes, higher tail latency, no confirmed data loss.

Nora: One quick wording change for the customer note: avoid saying "data loss" — say "no request payloads were dropped" if we can verify. Also recommend adding our engineering point of contact and timeline for follow-up (RCA + action plan in 3 business days).

Ravi: Confirmed — no payloads were dropped. We retried a handful of requests internally; all user inputs were persisted to logs and replays.

Maya: Draft status page update (short):
"Incident: Elevated latency in eu-west-1 — mitigated
Start: 2024-06-12 10:12 UTC
Resolved: 2024-06-12 10:45 UTC
Impact: Increased response times and intermittent timeouts for Dedicated customers in eu-west-1. Root cause: autoscaler configuration change combined with a traffic surge. Mitigation: reverted config, scaled capacity, applied cache eviction. Next steps: permanent autoscaler policy fix and improved traffic shaping controls."

Ana: SLA credit calc — based on SLA policy (monthly uptime / credits): For each affected customer I'll run their usage bucket but preliminary estimate: 1–3 days prorated credit depending on their committed capacity. Will confirm after telemetry check.

Devon: Preventative actions list (technical):
- Revert the scale-in cooldown change (done) and add automated guardrails to prevent risky config pushes without canary.
- Add a short-term autoscaler override rule for rapid bursts from single tenants.
- Tighten KV cache eviction thresholds and add better observability for cache pressure.
- Add a synthetic loadwork that simulates long-sequence bursts to catch this earlier in pre-prod.

Maya: For customer-facing follow-up, keep the actions high-level: "we will harden autoscaler controls, add improved monitoring and alerts for cache pressure, and provide an RCA with timeline and next steps within 3 business days." Add a note that their CS contact will share a credit estimate by EOD. :memo:

Ana: Draft outgoing message to customers (first pass):

"Hi — we wanted to follow up about the service disruption in eu-west-1 earlier today (10:12–10:45 UTC). You may have experienced increased response times and intermittent timeouts for Dedicated workloads. Our on-call and SRE teams identified an autoscaler configuration interaction with a traffic spike as the root cause. We mitigated the issue by reverting a recent autoscaler configuration change, scaling capacity, and performing targeted cache maintenance. There was no loss of customer request payloads. We’re taking steps to prevent recurrence (autoscaler guardrails, improved cache monitoring, and targeted load testing). We’ll share a more detailed RCA and a proposed timeline for permanent fixes within 3 business days. If you’d like to discuss impact or credits, please reply to this thread or reach out to your CS lead (Maya)."

Devon: Looks good. Minor edit: change "reverting the configuration change" -> "reverting a recent autoscaler configuration change".

Maya: I'll take the final pass for tone and send if everyone signs off. One more ask: include a short internal checklist for tracking follow-up items (assign owners + deadlines).

Ana: Creating ticket: CS-2467 (customer follow-ups & credit estimates) and ENG-9821 (RCA & preventative work). I'll assign owners and update here.

Ravi: I'll own ENG-9821 for the eng side. ETA for RCA doc draft: EOD +2 (two business days).

Nora: Can we also include a retro action to review our canary process for config pushes? Put that under ENG-9821 as well.

Maya: Final approvals? If no objections I’ll send the customer note and update the status page after Ana posts per-customer impact numbers. :eyes:

Ana: No objections from me. Sending the per-customer telemetry now and will ping when the final messages are ready. :white_check_mark:

Devon: Thx team — leaving a short note for on-call handoff: @Devon handing off to @Ravi at 18:00 UTC; watchlist: autoscaler metrics + cache eviction logs for 24h.

IncidentBot: [LOG] Incident #INC-2024-147 marked as post-incident review started by Ana.

Ana: (thread note) Attachments: I'll upload the per-customer request counts and a draft SLA credit table in CS-2467. If anyone wants to preview the customer emails before I send, ping me.
